According to Iroquois oral tradition, their ancestors came from the Great Lakes region, specifically from the area around Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. They migrated southward and eventually settled in the region around the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca, and Tuscarora rivers, which are now part of New York state.

The Iroquois people developed a complex society with a system of government, known as the "Great Law of Peace," which was established around 1570. This system of government was later adopted by the United States government and influenced the development of the US Constitution.
